title: Meeting Bill Russell and recording with Burbank, Wooden Joe and others
summary: Recalls recordings with Albert Burbank, Herb Morand, Wooden Joe, Big Eye Louis and Joe Nicholas around 1949, ending around Bunk Johnson's last illness.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah, I guess the first date that you made was there over at Albert Burbank. Also some with Wooden Joe that year, 1945.
I did too, that's right. And Big Eye Louie and Joe Nicholas. That's the records we...

I wasn't, let's see, I don't believe you made the records quite at 1950. Yeah. Push it. Well, we were just saying you started recording there with Albert Burbank. And there was that date you made with Herb Moran. And then you made some with Wooden Joe that year. Yeah, I cannot...
It was 1949, I guess, when we made those records.
Well, I can recall... I could remember definite about those records made because you should know the year good. The last record we made, Bonk Johnson was very sick.
And we, you had to leave, we made a rehearsal and you couldn't finish recording. Because you had to go...
Yeah, the next day Bonk died and I went over there.
Yeah, yeah. You say you want to be there when he died. And...
That's when we were recording Wooden Joe out there in his backyard that night. That's right.
Remember that? That's right. That's right. I remember that very well. No.
